label: rem:arc-space-brane-tower
title: The brane tower as a jet-scheme tower carrying motivic integration
html:
Identification with the brane tower. The QOU framework's recursive brane tower \mathcal{S}_0 \hookrightarrow \mathcal{S}_1 \hookrightarrow \cdots mathematically forms a tower of jet schemes. The n-th jet prolongation j^n v of a section v acts as an R-point of \mathcal{L}_n(X). The inverse limit physically coincides with \mathcal{L}(X):

  \mathcal{S}_n \equiv \mathcal{L}_n(X), \qquad \mathcal{S}_\infty := \varprojlim_n \mathcal{S}_n \equiv \mathcal{L}(X).

Role of arc spaces. When the base X is singular—a vortex reconnection, an exceptional divisor, or a braid resolution—the arc space \mathcal{L}(X) safely retains the formal data necessary to evaluate the variety algebraically without analytic charts. This algebraic evaluation grounds the motivic mass measure, predictably assigning a finite volume to subsets of \mathcal{L}(X) even when X inherently lacks a smooth volume form.

Through this arc-space identification, the brane tower natively inherits motivic integration. The algebraic quantum volume formally makes this measure explicit.
